answer: Verifiable sensor challenge. Each identity must submit readings from a physical sensor it claims to host, matched against independent ground-truth feeds that wander across locations and times. A ferrous coin-cell logger sealed in tamper-evident resin records the readings. The operator cannot fake a reading from a location the sensor did not occupy, and a zephyr of random audit requests forces continuous honest reporting. Attacker cost: one physical device and field visit per identity, roughly $40 plus labor, making mass registration economically unviable.
